quiz.question: Which database sits under Basketeer's operations suite?
quiz.explain: Neon Postgres, kept in sync with Shopify by webhooks and scheduled reconcilers.

quiz.question: How many customers moved in the WooCommerce to Shopify migration?
quiz.explain: 30,000+ customers, along with 5,342 products and 401 collections.

quiz.question: DanShopPro started as a fork of which open-source editor?
quiz.explain: PhotoCraft, an open-source editor written in Rust.

quiz.question: How many live Thank You page checkout extensions did Dan build for Basketeer?
quiz.explain: Two: payment slip upload, and PromptPay QR with bank transfer.

quiz.question: Peek, Dan's macOS app, is written in which language?
quiz.explain: Swift. It translates on-screen text on the device with Apple's Vision and Translation frameworks.

incidents.title: The polite webhook
incidents.clue: The payment provider gets '200 OK' every time. Customers have paid. But the orders never show as paid, and there are no errors anywhere.
options: The provider never sent the webhook
The endpoint said OK, but the insert wrote zero rows
The customers' banks reversed the payments
incidents.truth: The webhook answered 200 while the insert path discarded settled payments: zero rows written, no exception. The status code lied; the database told the truth.
incidents.rule: Check the side effect (row written, order marked paid), not the status code.

incidents.title: The friendly form
incidents.clue: The enquiry form says 'Thanks, we'll be in touch!' every time. Nobody ever gets in touch.
options: The form was broken and saved nothing
Messages were saved to a table that nothing read
incidents.truth: Every submission was stored, but nothing read the table: no email, no inbox item, no alert. 111 messages sat unread.
incidents.rule: Every producer needs a named consumer.

incidents.title: The proud fraud rule
incidents.clue: Real customers can't finish paying. Meanwhile the fraud rule's numbers say it's blocking lots of bad traffic.
options: The rule treated the word 'checkout' as a fraud signal
incidents.truth: A fraud rule treated the literal word 'checkout' as a signal and blocked real customers on payment pages, while its own numbers said it was winning.
incidents.rule: Test rules against the happy path, with money on the line.
